validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE, CLASSIFICATION AND NON-DUPLICATION ALL CONFIRMED, independent of GEM/wiki. Atlantic Bridge Phase 2 is a real, FERC-certificated (docket CP16-9, order issued 2017-01-19) interstate natural-gas expansion of the Algonquin Gas Transmission / Maritimes & Northeast systems, operated by Enbridge subsidiary Algonquin Gas Transmission, LLC. Corroborated across five independent lines: (1) Enbridge's own official project page (dead live, recovered via Wayback web.archive.org/web/20210619001447/); (2) NaturalGasIntel trade-press coverage of the FERC rehearing denial; (3) Utility Dive's 2017 coverage of the FERC approval (live URL 403s to a browser UA but the identical Wayback snapshot from 2017-02-15 -- three days after the article's own dateline -- confirms the content is genuine and contemporaneous, not a bot-wall fabrication); (4) 2b1stconsulting's 2015 pre-filing coverage; (5) JDSupra's legal-industry summary of the First Circuit's Weymouth Compressor Station air-permit litigation (Town of Weymouth v. MA DEP), which independently confirms the FERC certificate, the construction-authorization order (171 FERC P61,148), and the compressor-station dispute; (6) the EIA 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' historical workbook (government primary source), which carries THREE matching rows (Historical Projects sheet, rows 871/1014/1015) all keyed to 'Atlantic Bridge' under different operator/segment splits (Algonquin Gas Transmission LLC US-side lateral: Beg_State NJ / End_State MA, 6.3 mi / 42 in / $451.8M; and Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline LLC Canada-side: Beg_State MA / End_State NB, 0 new miles). Classification (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission) is correct and matches all sources. Not a duplicate of any other US-gas roster PID -- it is the correctly-scoped Phase 2 expansion of parent systems Algonquin (P0149) and Maritimes & Northeast (P0150), both already swept in batch 3; this row is properly a singleton segment on that swept system, not a re-listing of the parent trunks. CAVEAT (see the Location fill and its own validity/concern entry below): GEM's recorded Location fields (Massachusetts -> New Brunswick) trace to the EIA's separate Canada-side sub-project row, while the recorded physical specs (Length/Diameter/Cost) trace to the EIA's US-side lateral row (NJ->MA) -- i.e. GEM's single P1997 row characterizes the unified cross-border Phase 2 expansion using the US-side physical build specs plus the CAN-side jurisdictional endpoints. This is a defensible characterization (Enbridge's own materials describe Phase 2 as one project 'designed...to move...natural gas into New England and to specific end use markets in the Canadian Maritime provinces,' and NaturalGasIntel likewise describes gas flowing 'south-to-north into Canada'), not a duplicate or a fabricated row, but it is a genuine EIA-row conflation worth flagging for any future GEM segment-granularity review.

The sheet's recorded StartState/Province value 'Masschusetts' is a plain misspelling of Massachusetts -- confirmed against every independent source describing the project's New England / Weymouth (MA) footprint (Enbridge's own page: Weymouth Compressor Station, Massachusetts; JDSupra: 'Town of Weymouth, Massachusetts'; EIA workbook Beg_State/End_State fields use the standard 'MA' abbreviation). No source supports the literal spelling 'Masschusetts' as anything but a data-entry error. This is a mechanical correction, not a location dispute -- see the Location fill below for the broader EIA-row-conflation caveat, which is NOT contested here (EndState/Province='New Brunswick' is kept as recorded).

Per docs/reference/gem_schema.md, FuelSource must name a SPECIFIC upstream field/plant/facility, never a generic commodity type or a broad basin/region (the documented Saudi-sweep mistake where 12 'Natural Gas' fills had to be dropped). The only description found is 2b1stconsulting's characterization of the gas as sourced from 'the Marcellus and Utica basins' -- a broad multi-state shale-play region, not a named field/plant, so it does not meet the FuelSource naming bar. No source names a specific producing field, processing plant, or gathering facility feeding Atlantic Bridge Phase 2 (unsurprising -- it is a long-haul interstate transmission lateral moving already-processed pipeline-quality gas aggregated from many upstream Marcellus/Utica shippers under FERC open-season contracts, not a dedicated single-source lateral). Leaving genuinely UNRESOLVED rather than filling a basin name that would violate the schema convention.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Confirm operating. Firmest hard-dated evidence remains the Jan 25, 2021 full in-service declaration; no fresher (2022-2026) news story was located within this session's tool budget (WebSearch exhausted; WebFetch/curl/Wayback/Federal-Register-API used instead). Escalated: queried the Federal Register API directly for 'Algonquin Gas Transmission' + 'Atlantic Bridge' ordered newest-first -- the newest hit returned is the 2020-10-08 combined notice of FERC rate filings (RP21-4, Algonquin/M&NE 'Atlantic Bridge In-Service' filings effective 10/1/2020), i.e. no post-2021 FERC notice surfaced under that exact search term (the tariff schedule likely stopped using 'Atlantic Bridge' as a distinct rate-schedule label once folded into ordinary system rates after full in-service). Also re-fetched the live (non-Wayback) Enbridge URL directly during this pass -- confirmed HTTP 404, i.e. genuinely retired from the live site, not newly broken. Verdict 'confirm' is warranted despite the 2021-dated anchor because: (1) this is a certificated FERC interstate mainline (docket CP16-9) under continuous NGA tariff/rate-filing obligations, not a discretionary or news-cycle-dependent project; (2) no source of any kind (news, FERC docket activity, EIA data, litigation record) indicates the pipeline has been idled, abandoned, or decommissioned since reaching full in-service; (3) the parent Algonquin (P0149) and Maritimes & Northeast (P0150) systems, already swept in batch 3, remain active mainlines that this segment physically depends on and cannot be dormant independent of them. This reasoning, not a fresh annual news hit, is why 'confirm' rather than 'unclear' is staged.

summary: P1997 Atlantic Bridge Phase II is a real, well-documented, correctly classified FERC-certificated (CP16-9) operating expansion -- confirmed via 6 independent sources incl. EIA gov't data, and staged REFS_ADDED/fills on 13 of 15 units (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Proposal, Construction, Start+month, Capacity, Length, Diameter[medium/single-source], Location[typo-fixed], SegmentCost+year, Operator, Owner) plus 1 spec concern (typo Masschusetts->Massachusetts) and 1 caveat (GEM's row conflates the EIA's US-side physical-spec row with its Canada-side jurisdictional-endpoint row -- defensible, not an error, flagged for future segment-granularity review); UNRESOLVED: Pressure (no MAOP found anywhere) and FuelSource (only a broad Marcellus/Utica basin description exists, not a specific named facility per schema).
